register.name: US dollar bond tap, 10-year series
register.detail: Government Debt Management Agency (ÁKK) · February 2026 · reopens the 10-year US dollar bond series issued in summer 2025 · driven by reverse inquiry of investors
register.note: Part of the foreign-currency financing of the central budget in 2026
register.text: A tap of Hungary’s 10-year US dollar bond, placed in February 2026 at the request of investors. It finances the central budget, which pays for the public services behind the seven standards.

register.name: Eurobond issuance, including a green bond
register.detail: Government Debt Management Agency (ÁKK) · early January 2026 · €3bn in all, of which a €1bn green bond · significant investor demand
register.note: Green bonds were 4.95% of total debt at the end of June 2026
register.text: Hungary’s euro-denominated bond issuance of early January 2026, €3 billion in all, including a €1 billion green bond, which drew significant investor demand. It finances the central budget, which pays for the public services behind the seven standards.

register.name: Central government financing plan, 2026
register.detail: Government Debt Management Agency (ÁKK) · Debt Management Outlook 2026, December 2025 · gross issuance HUF 16,391bn · net foreign-currency issuance HUF 2,541bn (€6.5bn) · retail securities HUF 1,300bn
register.note: Total net funding requirement of the central budget; at 1 July 2026 the gross plan stood at HUF 16,797bn, 55.8% completed
register.text: The plan for financing Hungary’s central budget in 2026: a net funding requirement of HUF 5,445 billion, met by forint government bonds, retail securities and international bonds of up to €5.2 billion, including a benchmark-sized green Eurobond. It funds the central budget, which pays for the public services behind the seven standards.

register.name: Nyíregyháza water and wastewater system upgrades
register.detail: European Investment Bank · project 20240319 · approved 9 July 2025 · signed 5 November 2026 · borrower Municipality of Nyíregyháza · total cost HUF 139,290M (€348M)
register.note: Announced by the EIB on 6 November 2026 as €95.5M; the project page shows €96,370,946 signed, of up to HUF 69,000M (€172M) proposed
register.text: An EIB loan to the city of Nyíregyháza, a municipality of 120,000 people, to upgrade and expand its drinking water supply, sewerage, water reuse and stormwater management. It serves the water and shelter standards, with safe drinking water and sanitation for a growing city.

register.name: Student loans VII (Diákhitel Központ)
register.detail: European Investment Bank · project 20250251 · approved 6 May 2026 · signed 3 November 2026 · total cost about €294M
register.note: Project title: TechEU Diákhitel, Student Loan VII; the project also covers vocational training and adult learning
register.text: An EIB loan to Diákhitel Központ, Hungary’s student loan centre, to provide loans to students attending higher education institutions, and also vocational training and adult learning. It helps more people reach higher levels of education and serves the education standard.

register.name: Recovery and resilience plan
register.detail: Council of the EU · new plan submitted June 2026 · approved 10 July 2026 · about €6.5bn in grants and €3.5bn in loans · technical revision adopted in August 2026
register.note: The plan approved in December 2022 had €5.8bn in grants; the Commission’s annual report of 7 October 2026 lists Hungary among three Member States that had received less than 60% of their allocation
register.text: A new EU recovery and resilience plan for Hungary, approved by EU ministers on 10 July 2026, which should allow €10 billion to be disbursed against agreed reforms and investments. The Commission describes “a strong combination of reforms and targeted investment designed to address the country’s specific challenges”; on 29 May 2026 the Commission President said the agreed reforms unlock funding “frozen over the last years”.

register.name: EU cohesion policy, 2021–2027
register.detail: European Commission · Partnership Agreement adopted 22 December 2022 · ERDF €6.7bn · European Social Fund Plus €5.3bn · Cohesion Fund €1.7bn · Just Transition Fund over €250M
register.note: Almost €22 billion in all; on 29 May 2026 the Commission President announced €4.2bn of conditionality-related cohesion funds unlocked and a further €2.2bn to follow from reforms
register.text: EU cohesion funding for Hungary for 2021–2027, for better access to quality education, the integration of disadvantaged groups including Roma, the energy efficiency of buildings and water and wastewater management. In December 2022 the Council adopted measures under the Conditionality Regulation that included “a suspension of budgetary commitments from three operational cohesion programmes”; in 2026 the Commission proposed to lift those measures.

register.name: Renalfa solar and battery portfolio
register.detail: EBRD · 2026 · loan to special purpose vehicles owned by Renalfa IPP · part of a €210M package with commercial banks · 450 MW solar and 250 MW/1 GWh battery storage, northeastern Hungary
register.note: About 448 GWh of renewable electricity a year once operational; the EBRD has invested more than €3.7bn in Hungary across 220 projects
register.text: An EBRD loan for one of the largest renewable energy developments in Hungary, a solar portfolio with co-located battery storage built by Renalfa IPP, a joint venture of Renalfa Solarpro Group and RGREEN INVEST. It adds clean power and storage to the grid and serves the energy standard.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: Land that can feed the nation and earn abroad, valued and financed against its harvest.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 14.4% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Power from water, wind and sun already flows; every new connection can be clean.

items.name: Munch
items.text: A Hungarian company founded in 2020 whose app lets restaurants, bakeries and supermarkets sell their unsold food at reduced prices; it reports saving around HUF 8 billion of food, over 6.5 million portions, with 1,700 tonnes in 2024 alone, in Hungary, the Czech Republic, Slovakia and Romania.

items.name: Utcáról Lakásba! Egyesület (From Streets to Homes Association)
items.text: An association that runs the Hungarian version of Housing First and a social rental agency: private owners let their flats to it, it guarantees the rent and utility bills, renovates and maintains the homes and supports tenants with social workers; more than a hundred flats take part in its programmes and nearly 300 people live in flats it manages.

items.name: Igazgyöngy Alapítvány (Real Pearl Foundation)
items.text: A foundation set up in Berettyóújfalu in 1999 that works against child and intergenerational poverty through education, with an art school founded in 2000, family support, community development and income-generating ventures with families such as furniture making and textile embroidery; it works in Told and 17 other settlements and reaches over 1,200 families a year.

items.name: Nem Adom Fel Foundation
items.text: A foundation that gives people with disabilities jobs and supported living, with a café and restaurant in Budapest staffed mainly by people with disabilities, whose income funds its work; it employs 300 people with reduced work capacity.

items.name: Láthatatlan Kiállítás (Invisible Exhibition)
items.text: A ticketed exhibition in Budapest where blind and visually impaired guides lead visitors through rooms in complete darkness; it reopened on 8 July 2026, and in 2020 it described itself as a protected workplace where 25 of its 30 workers were blind or partially sighted.
